title: Snapshot Array
statement:
Implement an integer array that supports taking lightweight snapshots and querying any index as of a past snapshot.

Contract
- `new Solution(length)` creates an array of `length` elements (`length >= 1`), all initialized to `0`, at snapshot version `0`.
- `set(index, val)` updates element `index` (`0 <= index < length`) to `val` in the current unsealed version.
- `snap()` seals the current version, returns its snapshot ID (starting from `0` and increasing by `1` on each call), and advances to the next version.
- `get(index, snapId)` returns the value held at `index` when snapshot `snapId` was taken (`0 <= snapId < number of completed snaps`).
- Avoid copying the entire array on every `snap()`: store only actual mutations per index.

Examples
- With length `3`: `set(0, 5)`, `snap()` -> `0`, `set(0, 6)`, `get(0, 0)` -> `5`.
- Multiple writes before one snap overwrite the same version: `set(1, 2)`, `set(1, 9)`, `snap()` -> `0`, `get(1, 0)` -> `9`.
- Untouched indexes remain `0`: `snap()` -> `0`, `get(2, 0)` -> `0`.
hints: Copying the whole array on each snap() takes O(length * snaps) memory and time; instead, keep a history list of (snapId, value) pairs per index.
Because snapId only increases, each index's history list is naturally sorted by snapId; if set() is called multiple times at the same snapId, overwrite the last entry in place.

To answer get(index, snapId), binary search that index's history for the largest recorded version <= snapId. Intended complexity: O(1) amortized set/snap and O(log k) get (O(n log n) over n operations), with O(n) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: len N; op1, op2, ... where ops are set i v | snap | get i s, for example: len 3; set 0 5, snap, set 0 6, get 0 0
